accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England, English Appendix 2 (Year 6: subjunctive forms such as If I were or Were they to come in some very formal writing and speech) and its glossary entry for subjunctive (The school requires that all pupils be honest; The school rules demand that pupils not enter the gym at lunchtime; If Zoë were the class president, things would be much better). The base-form rules (no -s, be for every subject, not before the verb) and were for every subject in unreal conditions and wishes were checked in Cambridge English Grammar Today (Subjunctive) and the Merriam-Webster usage note. Real past conditions keep was (If he was late this morning, he missed the register), and everyday was and -s forms are presented as register choices, not errors.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: was in unreal conditions in formal writing (first prediction, m-items, challenge), over-using were for real past facts (When I was five, If he was late this morning, m2, challenge q4), treating every were as a subjunctive (Pupils were late on Monday prediction and letter step), adding -s, past tense or will after insist/suggest/recommend that (verb feedback map, challenge q2), doesn't or does not instead of not (fourth demand, challenge q6), and keeping if when inverting (If were they to win).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsubj combines a drag-was-or-were-into-the-gap step whose finished sentence is drawn inside a dashed dream cloud (imagined) or a solid box (real), a two-stage trigger-word-then-base-form step, a tap-the-pieces inversion builder with an If trap, a formal-letter spotter, and a formal/everyday shelf sort. No other flagship covers mood or the subjunctive; flagmodal, flagtense and flagvoice handle modal verbs, tense and voice. lab_distinct stayed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule by testing: dropping was into If I ___ a bird turns the card red with 'But this is imagined, not real. Formal writing uses were for every subject, even I and he', while was into When I ___ five turns blue and solid as a real fact. In the demand step the learner must first find the trigger word (insists, suggest, vital, demand) before the verb tiles appear, so the cause of the base form is discovered, not told. The inversion builder shows each partial build (Were they …) and the finished sentences stay on screen.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions carry the tempting wrong answer: 'was: I goes with was' for If I ___ a bird (the gap rejects was as imagined), 'is: he is one person' for The coach insists that he ___ on time (the verb tiles reject is and explain be), and 'Yes: it uses were' for Pupils were late on Monday (the letter step marks that line as a plain past fact).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve wrong-answer messages that each name the slip: was in a formal unreal condition, is for an unreal present, -s or will after recommend that, a plain past or real is mistaken for a subjunctive, were for a real past event, be outside a demand clause, keeping if in an inversion, a plain statement with no if, and don't or does not before the base form.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences with concrete cases (If I were a bird, I would fly. I am not a bird.) at FK grade 0.9 against the family kid target of 5.0. The adult text uses the precise terms subjunctive, base form, register and inversion at FK grade 9.0 against the 10.0 target.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation stayed under 12% six-word overlap with every lesson, including Grammar Terms: Modal Verbs and Clauses, Formal and informal English and Past, Present and Progressive Tense. Every lab message quotes the sentence the learner built or names the trigger word or verb form.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (touch, 1.5x) in light and dark before and after Show me: the was/were chips and dream-cloud cards fit, the trigger-word chips wrap onto two rows, the three verb tiles fit side by side, the inversion pieces sit in a 2x2 grid with 'to arrive early,' on two lines, all five letter lines fit, and both shelves hold three wrapped cards each. The inversion step's 'With if' line was moved down after the first screenshot showed it touching the step pill.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every canvas action has a labelled button ('Fill the gap with were', 'insists is the trigger word', 'Use be', 'Add Were next', 'Subjunctive in: …', 'If I were you, I would ask. is formal'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every message. A fuzz pass clicking every button in every step produced no console errors.

sources: National Curriculum in England: English Appendix 2 (Year 6) and Glossary: subjunctive
Cambridge Dictionary, English Grammar Today: Subjunctive
